title: Smart slab-split batcher for streaming completions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: implement a new batch formation heuristic tailored to streaming chat completions that simultaneously reduces tail latency, bounds GPU memory usage for KV cache, and improves token throughput under mixed SLAs.
description_details:
Background:
Current continuous-batcher groups streaming chat sessions by arrival time and affinity, but we observe two recurring problems: (1) bursty long-context sessions cause KV cache slabs to grow and force premature evictions, increasing token recomputation, and (2) naive coalescing of short interactive sessions into large micro-batches increases P99 latency for low-latency lanes.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a "slab-split" batcher that partitions incoming requests into two cooperating flows: the fast lane (latency-sensitive) and the throughput lane (throughput-optimized). Within the throughput lane, implement slab-aware grouping so that sessions with overlapping KV prefixes are coalesced into shared slabs; within the fast lane, enforce maximum micro-batch size and prefer sessions with hot KV pointers already resident on GPU. Add a lightweight scoring function that estimates per-request GPU memory delta (delta_kv), expected token cost, and stall risk. Use this score to decide (a) whether to place the request in the fast vs throughput lane, and (b) whether to trigger a shallow prefetch or defer and let it hit the fallback model variant.

Key heuristics (novel aspects):
- Slab split thresholding: rather than a single global slab, maintain per-shard slab targets that enforce headroom (watermark) proportional to 90th-percentile active context length per tenant. This prevents a single long-context session from starving slabs for other users.
- Soft pinning of very-hot KV ranges: dynamically detect KV blocks accessed >N times in the last M seconds and mark them soft-pinned so evictions prefer colder ranges; pinning decays exponentially to avoid long-term leaks.
- Prefetch budget buckets: allocate a tiny per-GPU ephemeral prefetch budget measured in bytes; scoring ensures prefetches are bounded and reclaimed when memory pressure spikes.
- Ragged-edge coalescing: when micro-batch fill time exceeds latency SLO for a request, cut the micro-batch and route remaining fillable requests to throughput lane rather than continuing to wait (reduces jitter and P99).
- Eviction patience windows: when memory pressure is transient, increase eviction patience for slabs that would cause recompute penalty >T tokens to avoid thrashing.

Operational constraints:
- Must not increase average memory footprint beyond 5% over baseline at peak.
- Fast lane P99 latency must hold within current SLO (e.g., 120ms for single-token streaming step) for 95% of tenants.
- New scoring code must be CPU-lightweight (target <2% CPU overhead on serving nodes).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Determining good defaults for soft-pin thresholds vs fairness across tenants. Potential mitigation: tenant-weighted slab quotas.
- Prefetch aggressiveness vs eviction churn: too-conservative prefetch hurts throughput; too-aggressive increases memory pressure. Plan to tune via staged canary.
- Interaction with model quantization (int8 kernels) and KV layout; certain quantized kernels may change memory/delta_kv calculations and require kernel-specific coefficients.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end bench: baseline vs slab-split batcher under mixed workload (50% short interactive, 30% medium, 20% long) shows >=8% throughput uplift for throughput lane without >5% avg GPU memory increase
Fast lane P99 single-token latency regresses by <=2% compared to baseline or stays within SLO (whichever is stricter)
KV eviction rate (evictions per 1k tokens) decreases for long-context-heavy tenants by >=20%
New scoring function CPU overhead <=2% measured over 1-hour soak at peak QPS
Feature gates and telemetry implemented: per-tenant lane assignment, slab usage histograms, prefetch budget exhaustion counters

notes: Implementation plan: 1) scoring hook and lane assignment (2 weeks), 2) per-shard slab targets + soft pin (2 weeks), 3) prefetch budget enforcement + telemetry (1 week), 4) canary and tuning (2 weeks)
Rollout: gated by feature flag; start canary on non-production region, then low-traffic tenants, then 10% global, 50%, GA. Monitor eviction_rate, slab_headroom, and P99 latency closely.
Related experiments: compare static tenant slab quotas vs adaptive slab headroom; evaluate with and without shallow prefetch.
